census_contract.over_bound_behavior: refuses with 'linux process census exceeds its bound' rather than truncating
census_contract.why_defunct_follows_session: Linux getsid(2) succeeds on an unreaped task because the task struct survives until reaped, so a zombie still reports the session it belonged to and would otherwise be named as a live member
census_contract.why_hook_shape: a file tagged darwin or linux cannot reference the Darwin-only darwinProcessZombie constant, and Linux's three dead-but-unreaped states cannot be expressed as one comparison against a uint32 status; the hook returns defunct, present and error so a vanished lifetime is omitted while a denial or malformed record refuses rather than guessing liveness

supervision forking a child that can itself become a member of the session it is draining

the mechanism is a deliberate race the test constructs: it launches /bin/sh -c '/bin/sh -c "sleep 1; exec /usr/bin/git hash-object --stdin" child <&3 & wait' and polls every 20ms for the other-to-git exec transition, so the sampler walks the tree at the instant sleep 1 exits. A descendant that exits is simultaneously reparented, which breaks the parent-equality half of linuxProcessResidentBytes' zero-RSS recovery condition and turns a missing smaps_rollup into the hard error; collectLinuxResidentObservation retries only errLinuxProcessNameTransition, and the test's own table pins {'missing memory', os.ErrNotExist, 'name', 1, true}

newly_named_prerequisite.name: Linux immutable-flag input-custody model
newly_named_prerequisite.finding: Linux FS_IMMUTABLE_FL via FS_IOC_SETFLAGS requires CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE; there is no unprivileged owner-set immutable equivalent to Darwin's unix.Fchflags(UF_IMMUTABLE). inputCustodyOwned, inputCustodyProtected, inputCustodyFlag and inputCustodyVolume are therefore refusal stubs on Linux, and ProtectExecutionGoBuildInputs plus the whole zoekt-offer native build path cannot run here.
newly_named_prerequisite.why_it_matters: it is a genuine design question rather than a port: the options are a granted capability, a read-only bind mount, a user namespace, or an explicitly weaker documented custody model, and each has a different adversary.
newly_named_prerequisite.backlog_status: was not named in the remaining-H2-prerequisites list before this slice; it is now recorded in docs/BACKLOG.md under T42.H2f and T42.H2g.

cost_pass: No new per-query/request, sync tick, startup/restart, retry/no-op or publication work; ordinary runtime is unchanged and no production dispatch site is added or removed. The changed path is supervision-only and runs at the existing ten-millisecond poll cadence and five-second custody-command deadline. Per poll the syscall order is unchanged while one child process, one pipe and one 128-KiB text parse are removed and the two-second probe context disappears because no child bounds it: the loop is bounded by construction at 8192 listing entries, at most 8192 getsid calls of roughly 200ns each, and at most 1024 session members each costing one /proc/<pid>/stat read plus one confirming getsid. Reading /proc/<pid>/stat field 6 instead of getsid was rejected on cost, at two to five microseconds per candidate versus roughly 200 nanoseconds, over every host PID at ten milliseconds. No numeric sort was added because order is not load-bearing in any of the three callers and the Darwin census is unsorted too; the empty census now returns an empty non-nil slice rather than nil, and all three callers are nil-insensitive. No lock is held across the census, no new persistent state exists, and no cache is invalidated.
